question: The first anonymous 1711-row development result corrected 67 but spoiled 50. Does the same autonomous mechanism outperform its own protected model again on a completely disjoint set of shared-title components, without supplying the initially accepted method or weight?
design: Registered on the first anonymous result and the Wine check, independently of any course raw prediction comparison. Use the next, second, fold of the same fixed five-fold grouped assignment and exactly the first run's recruitment runtime and generic Arctic-inclusive resources. Verify both the first held-index fingerprint and zero common title groups between the two audited panels. Build a new cold task packet and restrict any reusable pointwise embeddings to that run's training texts. Train a single ordinary course solver with 32 fits and 1800 seconds, no model, prior runs, previous errors or planner hints. Keep its actual full-data incumbent. Require native reload of the candidate and independent incumbent output, before seeing any new held answers. This is a replication on the known training corpus, with overlapping fitting examples between runs.
decision: Report the entire new panel even in the event of retention, regression or no reachable nominee. Report raw corrections, regressions, absolute accuracy, grouping interval, and pooled paired net count across the two mutually exclusive held panels. Require positive net in both panels and at least +0.20 points pooled over the same runs' own incumbents to justify studying broader autonomous adoption. A tie can show protection but does not establish repeated benefit. Do not use the second panel to select an alternative recipe or to change this runtime.
usage: One new cold run, at most 32 real local fits. Do not repeat the separate previous-controller control or the Wine test. No model API, no designated course validation, official test or H2.
